newsitem.title: FRANCE: MOTOR RACING-ESTORIL REPLACED BY JEREZ ON F1 CALENDAR.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-ESTORIL REPLACED BY JEREZ ON F1 CALENDAR.

text.p: This year's Portuguese Grand Prix has been cancelled and replaced by a race at the Spanish circuit at Jerez after doubts were raised over the completion of work at Estoril, it was announced on Thursday.

In a statement from their Paris headquarters, the sport's ruling body, the Federation Internationale de l'Automobile (FIA), said the event at Jerez will be known as the European Grand Prix. It will take place on October 26, the date scheduled originally for the Portuguese round of the championship until it was called off.

The FIA said it was hopeful that Portugal would regain a place on the Formula One calendar in the future when the scheduled improvements to the circuit, including alterations to the paddock and various spectator facilities, as well as enhanced run-off areas, were completed.
It is understood that no date for completion of the work had been satisfactory stated to the FIA.

Jerez has not hosted a Formula One Grand Prix since 1994 when it was the venue for the European Grand Prix won by Michael Schumacher in a Benetton on his way to his first world drivers' title. Schumacher had returned after a two-race ban during which rival Briton Damon Hill won twice for Williams.

The F1 season usually ends in Japan or Australia but was this year scheduled to close in Europe - originally in Portugal - at the special request of Renault, who are withdrawing from F1 at the end of the year.
